slides.title: Never order a “pepperoni” pizza.
slides.sub: Unless you really, really love bell peppers.

slides.heading: Peperoni means peppers.
paragraphs: In Italian, peperoni are bell peppers. Red, yellow, green. Zero salami.
Order a “pepperoni pizza” and you'll get exactly what you asked for. Just not what you wanted.

slides.heading: Ask for a Diavola.
paragraphs: The “devil's pizza”: tomato, mozzarella and spicy salami — salame piccante.
It's the closest thing to American pepperoni. And it's on almost every menu.

slides.heading: Survive the menu
items: Spicy salami. The one you were looking for.

slides.heading: One pizza, one person.
paragraphs: In an Italian pizzeria, everyone orders a whole pizza. Just for themselves.
Sharing is optional. Finishing it is expected.

slides.title: Tag the friend who orders pepperoni.
slides.text: Follow for Italian Rule Nº 5 — the pineapple question. We're ready. Are you?

caption:
Italian Rule Nº 4 🍕
Never order a “pepperoni” pizza in Italy.

Peperoni = bell peppers. If you want spicy salami, ask for a Diavola. Your taste buds will thank you. Your waiter will respect you.

Has this ever happened to you? 👇

—
🇮🇹 Regola italiana n.4: i “pepperoni” americani da noi si chiamano salame piccante. Quanti turisti avete visto cadere nella trappola?
